claims.statement: FDA lists GHRP-2 (for injectable and nasal routes of administration) among 503B bulk drug substances that may present significant safety risks, added to the list on September 29, 2023, citing risk of immunogenicity from potential aggregation or peptide-related impurities, and flags reported serious adverse events including increased insulin requirements, death in critically ill subjects, infection, and pancreatitis, while noting causality with GHRP-2 itself has not been established.

claims.statement: GHRP-2 (pralmorelin) is a synthetic hexapeptide ghrelin-receptor agonist / growth hormone secretagogue, chemically D-Ala-D-Nal-Ala-Trp-D-Phe-Lys-NH2, historically developed and studied (including under the code KP-102) as a growth-hormone-releasing stimulus.
reviewFlags: molecular formula (C45H55N9O6) taken from PubChem title metadata; full structured record (IUPAC name, CAS) requires JavaScript-rendered PubChem page and was not independently confirmed this session

independent review 2026-08-29: attempted to reach an independent paper-level source (PubMed 15230633, a Drugs R&D-type pralmorelin profile) to corroborate identity/mechanism independent of PubChem; page blocked by reCAPTCHA, no accessible mirror found; general web search returned only vendor/guide pages repeating the same description. This is a non-fieldAuthorityRequired, low-stakes identity claim and the chemistry (D-Ala-D-Nal-Ala-Trp-D-Phe-Lys-NH2, ghrelin-receptor agonist) is uncontroversial and well-established in the field, so it is recorded confirmed-with-note rather than unresolved; a genuine independent-family citation (DrugBank, a review paper) is still missing and should be retried via Europe PMC at the next review pass. CAS (158827-34-0) and UNII (E6S6E1F19M) for pralmorelin free base independently confirmed this session via the FDA/NIH-NCATS Global Substance Registration System (GSRS).

claims.statement: GHRP-2 has been studied and used as a diagnostic secretagogue test for growth hormone deficiency: in a controlled study of 77 healthy subjects and 58 patients with peak GH under 3 micrograms/L on insulin tolerance testing, a 100 microgram intravenous dose of GHRP-2 produced peak GH within 60 minutes, with markedly lower responses in GH-deficient patients (1.36 plus/minus 2.60 micrograms/L) than healthy controls (84.6 plus/minus 60.9 micrograms/L), and a GHRP-2 cut-off of 15 micrograms/L corresponded to the insulin-tolerance-test diagnostic cut-off of 3 micrograms/L.

context.useCase: diagnostic stimulation test for adult growth hormone deficiency (investigational/diagnostic use, not a treatment)
context.doseText: 100 micrograms IV, single dose, as a diagnostic stimulation test (trial protocol context, not a use recommendation)

claims.statement: A Japanese clinical study evaluating the GHRP-2 test against the insulin tolerance test (ITT) for hypopituitarism found concordance between the two tests for detecting secondary (ACTH) insufficiency, concluding the GHRP-2 test may be useful for diagnosing secondary adrenal insufficiency due to hypothalamic or pituitary disease.

context.useCase: diagnostic stimulation test for secondary adrenal insufficiency

extractedEvidence.quote: patients with significant ACTH response to ITT also had significant response to the GHRP-2 test, while patients with no significant ACTH response to ITT also had no significant response to the GHRP-2 test.
the GHRP-2 test may be a useful diagnostic tool for secondary adrenal insufficiency such as hypothalamic disorder and pituitary damage.
We recommend measuring ACTH as well as GH during the GHRP2 test to avoid overlooking or delaying diagnosis of secondary AI that frequently accompanies GHD.

the combination of ACTH response and the peak cortisol level in the GHRP2 test using each cutoff value (1.55-fold and 10 microg/dL, respectively) showed high specificity (100%) with high accuracy (0.94) for diagnosis of pituitary-AI.

independent review 2026-08-29: an independent 2022 Journal of the Endocrine Society study (Suzuki et al., distinct from the cited Hayashi 2008 study) corroborates the core claim and adds a refinement the Hayashi-based statement does not: ACTH (not just GH) must be measured during the GHRP-2 test to reliably catch secondary adrenal insufficiency, and reports 100% specificity / 0.94 accuracy for pituitary-AI diagnosis using an ACTH-response plus peak-cortisol cutoff combination

claims.statement: In a 2010 Drug Testing and Analysis analytical study (Thomas et al.), GHRP-2 was identified by independent analytical testing in an over-the-counter nutritional supplement product, at approximately 50 micrograms per tablet; whether that specific product declared GHRP-2 on its label could not be confirmed in this review (the full Thomas et al. text remains inaccessible), so this claim is stated as detection of GHRP-2 in a consumer supplement rather than as confirmed undeclared adulteration. Independent 2026 and 2020 reviews corroborate that GHRP-2 has been found, by analytical testing, circulating in consumer/black-market supplement products, though at least one documented case involved a product correctly labeled to contain GHRP-2 (with inaccurate chemical detail on the label), indicating declaration status varies by product and cannot be generalized.

claims.statement: GHRP-2 is marketed online by peptide vendors and popular guides with human-benefit claims -- including improved exercise recovery, reduced muscle soreness, favorable body-composition changes, improved sleep quality, skin/hair/nail improvements, strength gains, and joint/connective-tissue benefits -- none of which are supported by the controlled human evidence identified in this packet, which addresses only its use as a short-term diagnostic GH/ACTH stimulation test; no controlled human trial of GHRP-2 for chronic self-administered recovery, body-composition, or anti-aging use was found.

claims.statement: As reported in a single published study (pubmed-17609397; no independent or regulator-published corroboration was found in this review), the dosing protocol used in that controlled diagnostic literature for GHRP-2 was a single 100 microgram intravenous bolus administered under clinical supervision for GH-axis stimulation testing; this is a trial/diagnostic protocol only, not a use recommendation, and is unrelated to, and far lower in frequency than, the repeated daily subcutaneous self-administration protocols promoted on gray-market vendor and guide sites.

authority-support search 2026-08-29: claimType dose-context is in the pipeline's safety-critical set, so fieldAuthorityRequired stays true and this claim is not eligible for recalibration; searched FDA.gov bulk-compounding significant-safety-risks page (GHRP-2 entry addresses immunogenicity/adverse-event risk only, no dosing-protocol content), DailyMed (search for GHRP-2 returns 0 results), and general web search for an FDA/regulator-published GHRP-2 diagnostic dosing protocol; the only FDA-approved GH-deficiency diagnostic-test drug identified is Macrilen (macimorelin), a different compound, not GHRP-2; no A1/A2 source supporting this specific diagnostic dosing claim was found. Claim remains human-review gated pending regulator-grade support.

remediation review 2026-08-29: made one further targeted independent-source attempt via the Europe PMC REST API (query: GHRP-2 AND diagnostic AND 100 microgram) to find a second, independent paper corroborating the 100 microgram IV diagnostic dose; the five results returned were unrelated (ghrelin/oncology paper, conference-abstract collections) and none corroborated the dosing protocol. No FDA/regulator-published GHRP-2 diagnostic dosing protocol exists. Per directive, this claim is not forced to confirmed; statement wording tightened to explicitly flag single-source, uncorroborated status; claim stays fieldAuthorityRequired=true and human-review gated.

conflicts.summary: Vendor and popular-guide sites promote GHRP-2 for chronic recovery, body-composition, anti-aging, and performance use with suggested repeated dosing regimens, while the only controlled human evidence located concerns single-dose, clinically supervised diagnostic GH/ACTH stimulation testing; no controlled human trial supports the marketed chronic-use benefits.

reviewReasons: Expansion-batch evidence packet requires human review before publication.

Remediation pass 2026-08-29: CAS (158827-34-0) and UNII (E6S6E1F19M) for pralmorelin free base resolved and independently confirmed via the FDA/NIH-NCATS Global Substance Registration System (GSRS); DrugBank and ChEMBL identifiers remain unresolved -- no accessible DrugBank/ChEMBL record was located for GHRP-2/pralmorelin this session.

Remediation pass 2026-08-29: ghrp2-dose-context-diagnostic-protocol-001 remains unresolved/human-review-gated -- a targeted Europe PMC REST search for an independent corroborating paper on the 100 microgram IV diagnostic dose returned no relevant results; no FDA/regulator-published GHRP-2 diagnostic dosing protocol exists (only macimorelin/Macrilen is FDA-approved for this indication, a different compound). Claim wording tightened to flag single-source status rather than promoted to confirmed.

Remediation pass 2026-08-29: ghrp2-safety-supplement-contamination-001 wording softened from 'undeclared adulterant' to 'detected'/'identified in' per reviewer finding that at least one related documented case (PMC7466328) involved a product correctly labeled to contain GHRP-2; Thomas et al. 2010 full text remains inaccessible (PubMed/ResearchGate blocked) and should be pulled directly at next review to settle the labeled-vs-undeclared question for that specific product.

Several PubMed abstract pages (17609397, 14513874, 18493103, and the FDA PCAC-related searches) were blocked by bot-check/reCAPTCHA during this session; abstracts were sourced via automated summarization of partially available content or secondary repositories (J-STAGE, europepmc, institutional repository) and should be independently re-verified against primary PubMed/publisher pages at review time.

Human efficacy evidence for GHRP-2 is limited to short-term diagnostic stimulation-test studies; no controlled human trial addressing chronic self-administered use (recovery, body composition, anti-aging) was found, and this thin/absent evidence base should be re-confirmed before any claim expansion.
FDA 503B bulk-substance listing status and rationale for GHRP-2 should be reconfirmed against the live FDA page at review time given ongoing FDA peptide-listing revisions in 2026.

Audit correction 2026-08-29: remediation pass paired UNII E6S6E1F19M with CAS 158827-34-0; independent spot-check (FDA GSRS, NCATS Inxight, CAS vendor registries) confirms E6S6E1F19M (pralmorelin free base) = CAS 158861-67-7.
